parts.text:
4
A school has a piece of aluminium that it uses for radioactivity experiments. Its thickness is
marked as 3.2 mm. A student decides to check this value. He has vernier calipers which give
measurements to 0.1 mm and a micrometer which gives measurements to 0.01 mm.
Which statement must be correct?
A
The micrometer gives a more accurate measurement.
B
The micrometer gives a more precise measurement.
C
The vernier calipers give a more accurate measurement.
D
The vernier calipers give a more precise measurement.

hints: Notice the word must and the two least counts given for checking the $3.2\text{ mm}$ thickness: $0.1\text{ mm}$ and $0.01\text{ mm}$.
Recall that precision relates to resolution and fineness of reading, while accuracy means closeness to the true value.
Ask whether a finer scale alone guarantees freedom from zero error or closeness to $3.2\text{ mm}$, and which instrument must give the finer reading.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: true marked thickness about $3.2\text{ mm}$, vernier calipers to $0.1\text{ mm}$, micrometer to $0.01\text{ mm}$.
State the definitions: precision describes the fineness of the scale and repeatability, linked to least count; accuracy describes how close a reading is to the true value.
Compare resolution: $0.01\text{ mm}$ is ten times smaller than $0.1\text{ mm}$, so the micrometer can distinguish smaller differences in thickness.
Explain accuracy: closeness to the true value depends also on calibration and zero error, which are not given, so neither instrument is guaranteed to be more accurate.
Conclude that only the statement about finer resolution must hold, so the micrometer must give the more precise measurement. This is option B.

A.explanation: A smaller least count does not guarantee closeness to the true $3.2\text{ mm}$ value, as a zero error could still make the micrometer reading inaccurate.

B.explanation: The micrometer reads to $0.01\text{ mm}$ compared with $0.1\text{ mm}$ for the calipers, so its smaller least count gives finer resolution and greater precision.

C.explanation: Accuracy cannot be decided from resolution alone, so there is no reason the $0.1\text{ mm}$ vernier calipers must be closer to the true thickness.

D.explanation: The vernier calipers have the larger least count of $0.1\text{ mm}$, so they are less precise than the $0.01\text{ mm}$ micrometer.
